## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized mason wasp characterized by its black body with pale yellow or whitish markings, narrow waist, folded wings, and compact, solitary-wasp appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, yards, and other open or semi-open habitats with flowers, shrubs, and nesting cavities. Females use preexisting holes, hollow stems, or small cavities for nests, stocking them with paralyzed caterpillars or other soft-bodied larvae for their young, while adults visit flowers for nectar and help control herbivorous insects.
